title: Bài sưu tầm 132 - Passage 1: Coober Pedy: Life Beneath the Australian Outback
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 132

Coober Pedy: Life Beneath the Australian Outback

Paragraph 1. Across the treeless red plains of South Australia, summer temperatures routinely soar past forty-five degrees Celsius, making outdoor shelter nearly unbearable. Yet beneath this harsh desert sits Coober Pedy, the world's opal capital. The settlement began by chance in 1915, when fourteen-year-old Willie Hutchison wandered from his father's gold-prospecting camp while searching for drinking water and stumbled upon glittering seams of opal instead.

Paragraph 2. Word spread quickly, and by 1919 returning soldiers from the First World War flocked to the isolated field. Timber and corrugated iron were expensive to haul across the outback and offered poor protection against blistering days and freezing winter nights. Taking inspiration from abandoned burrows, the ex-soldiers cut living quarters directly into the pale, soft sandstone ridges, a practice that inspired the town's local name from an Indigenous phrase meaning 'white man in a hole'.

Paragraph 3. Known as 'dugouts', these underground homes offer surprising comfort. Because thick rock walls block extreme external heat, interior rooms stay at a steady twenty-three degrees Celsius all year, sparing residents the heavy electricity bills of mechanical cooling. However, carving into rock requires careful airflow design: builders bore narrow upright vents straight up to the surface so fresh air circulates continuously and excess humidity escapes.

Paragraph 4. Over decades, residents expanded underground life far beyond basic bedrooms, excavating churches, bookshops, and even hotels into the hillsides. Above ground, the dry landscape prevents natural lawns from growing, yet locals still maintain a famous golf course. To escape daytime glare, players tee off after sunset using glowing balls and carry a small square of artificial turf to place beneath each shot across the stony ground.

Paragraph 5. Mining itself has evolved dramatically since the era of handheld picks and candles. Contemporary crews operate truck-mounted suction machines, nicknamed blowers, to draw loose rubble and dust up from deep workings. At the same time, a century of digging has left a treacherous legacy: the surrounding desert is dotted with thousands of unmarked, abandoned mining shafts, posing a serious hazard to careless visitors who wander off marked tracks.

Paragraph 6. As shallow opal seams become harder to find and fuel expenses climb, the town increasingly relies on heritage tourism and science-fiction film shoots attracted to its lunar scenery. Even residents who can afford modern surface houses often prefer staying below ground, insisting nothing matches the total silence and restful sleep found behind solid rock walls.

groups.instructions:

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 2: "cut living quarters directly into the pale, soft sandstone ridges" (slopes = ridges).
Đoạn 3: "builders bore narrow upright vents straight up to the surface" (vertical = upright).
Đoạn 4: "carry a small square of artificial turf" (synthetic = artificial; portable patch = small square).
Đoạn 5: "operate truck-mounted suction machines... to draw loose rubble and dust up".
Đoạn 5: "thousands of unmarked, abandoned mining shafts" (unguarded old = unmarked, abandoned).
Đoạn 6: "nothing matches the total silence and restful sleep".

q8.text: Willie Hutchison was searching for gold when he came across the first opals at Coober Pedy.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bố cậu tìm vàng (gold-prospecting camp), còn bản thân Willie đi tìm nước uống (searching for drinking water) thì tình cờ thấy đá opal.

q9.text: Indigenous Australians actively helped returning soldiers excavate the earliest underground homes.

steps: Đoạn 2: Bài nhắc tên thị trấn bắt nguồn từ cụm từ của người bản địa và nhắc cựu binh đào nhà ngầm, nhưng không nói người bản địa có trực tiếp giúp đào hay không.

q10.text: Residents in underground homes depend heavily on electric cooling during summer.

steps: Đoạn 3: Tường đá dày giữ nhiệt độ ổn định 23°C quanh năm, giúp cư dân không tốn tiền điện chạy máy lạnh (sparing residents the heavy electricity bills of mechanical cooling).

q11.text: Games at Coober Pedy's golf course take place after dark.

steps: Đoạn 4: "players tee off after sunset using glowing balls" (chơi sau khi mặt trời lặn với bóng phát sáng).

q12.text: Modern opal mining relies on specialized machinery to lift waste soil out of underground workings.

steps: Đoạn 5: Đội khai thác hiện đại dùng máy hút gắn trên xe tải để hút đất đá vụn từ hầm sâu lên.

q13.text: Income from film productions now exceeds the money generated by opal sales in Coober Pedy.

steps: Đoạn 6: Bài có nói thị trấn dựa vào du lịch và quay phim khoa học viễn tưởng khi trữ lượng opal giảm, nhưng hoàn toàn không so sánh doanh thu giữa quay phim và bán opal.
